prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In frames 1–4, the depth map lays out a desk area in the lower-left foreground (~0.6–0.9 m away, within arm's reach of the camera wearer) with a mug and speaker, a wall-mounted whiteboard above and behind the desk (~1.0–1.3 m away), a partially cut-off monitor on the far left (~1.0–1.2 m away), and a black cat on a right-side windowsill (~0.8–1.1 m from the wearer and ~0.5 m right of the desk items). Across frames 1 to 4, the cat drops from standing upright with its front paw reaching the lower-right edge of the whiteboard down into a crouch on the sill, before the camera wearer turns sharply left in frame 5. Frame 5 reveals a person in the lower-left foreground (~0.8 m away, within the wearer's arm's reach) facing right in profile toward two side-by-side monitors (~1.2–1.5 m away, within that person's arm's reach) and away from the camera wearer, while the whiteboard shifts to the far right edge (~1.5 m away) and the person's lower body is cut off below the frame. Compared to RGB, the depth map clearly separates the dark silhouette of the black cat from the window blinds behind it and distinguishes the foreground desk clutter and person's head from the receding walls and monitors. However, the map is unreliable in frames 1–2 where bright depth bleeding flattens the boundary between the cat, desk, and lower whiteboard, and in frame 5 where the upper-right fisheye corner is erroneously rendered pure white (nearest) and the corner walls behind the monitors drop into an artificially deep black void.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the black cat on the right windowsill (~0.8–1.1 m away) as a single mask that lowers from reaching up onto the bottom-right corner of the whiteboard in frames 1–2 to crouching on the sill in frames 3–4, while also labeling the cup (~0.7 m away, within the wearer's arm's reach) on the lower-left desk and the partially visible monitor on the far left (~1.0–1.2 m away). When the camera wearer pans left in frame 5, the cat disappears out of view to the right, and the map segments a person on the lower left (~0.8 m away, torso cropped by the bottom edge) facing right away from the camera wearer toward two adjacent monitors (~1.2–1.5 m ahead of the wearer and ~0.5–0.7 m in front of the person, within the person's arm's reach) that slightly overlap at their inner bezel. The sharp mask contours clarify the exact silhouette of the black cat's paw overlapping the whiteboard lip in frames 1–2 and cleanly partition the two adjacent monitors and the person's profile in frame 5 despite low contrast and screen glare in the RGB image. However, the map is unreliable where it misclassifies the wall-mounted whiteboard (~1.0–1.3 m away, above the desk) as a 'tv' in frames 1–3 before dropping its mask entirely in frames 4–5, hallucinates a tiny 'mouse' next to the cup in frame 4, and misses the window blinds, desk surface, and tabletop speakers across all frames.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank across frames 1–3 because no human body parts are sufficiently visible in the scene while the camera faces the whiteboard and cat. In frame 4, a small cluster of yellow keypoints appears at the bottom-right edge (~0.8–1.0 m away, near the windowsill), where the estimator falsely triggers on the crouching black cat's silhouette and the dark fur/fabric edge in the extreme lower-right foreground. In frame 5, after the camera turns left, yellow keypoints mark the head (ear, eye, nose) and shoulders of the person in the lower-left foreground (~0.8 m from the camera wearer), whose torso and arms are occluded below the bottom frame boundary. These facial and shoulder landmarks explicitly confirm that the person's head is oriented to the right in profile, looking toward the dual monitors (~0.5–0.7 m ahead of them) and not toward the camera wearer. While the pose map makes the person's rightward head orientation and shoulder axis explicit in frame 5, it is unreliable in frame 4 due to the false-positive skeleton on the cat and provides no hand keypoints (magenta) in any frame because everyone's hands are out of view below the framing.
